description:
What is awkward: pkix-aia/src/lib.rs:566 declares fn fetch(&self, uri: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, AiaError>. The caching-wrapper doctest at lines 503-525 stores Result<Vec<u8>, AiaError> in a BTreeMap and clones the entry on every replay. For a multi-KiB cert response, every cache hit allocates and copies.

The trait design admits caching by the &self choice and the Clone+Eq+Send+Sync invariant on AiaError (great — see PKIX-o3op-G2). But the byte payload itself is owned-Vec, so every cache hit pays an allocation+copy.

Suggested rewrite: not the trait signature itself — Vec<u8> as the return type is the right call (ownership transfer to the caller who will parse it; aligns with raw-bytes-not-parsed-certs principle stated in rustdoc lines 437-443). But the rustdoc-level commentary should:

(a) State explicitly that caching wrappers wanting zero-copy replay should wrap the inner fetcher with their own Arc<[u8]> indirection — the trait returns owned bytes so the caller's wrapper can choose ownership shape downstream.
(b) Optionally include this as a second doctest, or amend the existing CachingFetcher doctest with a comment noting the Clone cost.

This is a defensible-design-decision finding more than a code defect. The current design is correct; it just doesn't document why. Without explanation, a future contributor might propose 'return Arc<[u8]>' or 'return Cow<'a, [u8]>' and the maintainer will have to re-derive the rationale.
title: AiaFetcher returns Vec<u8>: caching wrappers must Clone the bytes per replay
